newsitem.title: CANADA: FIGURE SKATING-GERMANS WIN PAIRS TITLE AT SKATE CANADA.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-GERMANS WIN PAIRS TITLE AT SKATE CANADA.

text.p: Germany's Mandy Woetzel and Ingo Steuer edged Russian world champions Marina Eltsova and Andrei Bushkov in a sloppy free-skating final to win the pairs title Friday at Skate Canada.
Russian judge Tatiano Danilenko cast the deciding vote in the Germans' favour as Woetzel and Steuer waltzed away with the $30,000 top prize.
Woetzel and Steuer omitted a scheduled throw triple toe loop after Steuer lost his grip on Woetzel's waist and she never got off the ice.
"We skated better in practice," said Steuer. "The results were a surprise."
The world champions were left with the second prize of $18,000. Americans Kyoko Ina and Jason Dungjen collected $10,000 for third place.
Eltsova and Bushkov, who nipped the Germans for gold at the 1996 worlds in Edmonton, led after Thursday's short programme and followed them Friday night in position to clinch another victory.
But they both crashed to the ice on their side-by-side triple jumps, then Bushkov fell again later in the programme.
Fourth place went to Canadians Kristy Sargeant and Kris Wirtz, who were openly critical of the quality of the ice.
Sargeant said there were holes so deep in the ice that in places she could see the cement floor. "A good description of the ice is that it's like peanut brittle," said Wirtz.
Germans Peggy Schwarz and Mirko Muller withdrew after Muller was cut across the left eyebrow by Schwarz's elbow during their four-minute presentation.
In the ice dance event, world bronze medalists Shae-Lynn Bourne Victor Kraatz were judged to have the best compulsory, the Golden Waltz. The original dances are Saturday and the free dance is Sunday.
In women's singles, Irina Slutskaya of Russia led after the short programme, with Yulia Vorobieva of Azerbaijan second and American Tara Lipinski third.
Lu Chen of China, the top-ranked skater in the field at number two in the world, withdrew earlier in the day after aggravating a foot injury in practice.

The men's event winds up on Saturday. Canadian Elvis Stojko, the 1994 and 1995 world champion, has the lead going into the free-skating final with Ilia Kulik of Russia and American Michael Weiss close behind.
